transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this pre-job review together because we need to discuss the solvent-recovery trial for the new skid beside the coating area. As you know, we have nine hundred liters of solvent mixture in drums awaiting a disposition decision, and the skid is installed but hasn't been used on production solvent yet. Before I can authorize anything, we need to go through the standard pre-job requirements together: equipment inspection, closed transfer, ventilation verification, vapor monitoring, and documented waste handling. I'd like to hear from each of you on where we stand. Let's start with process engineering — can you walk us through the current status of the skid and the recovery process?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to share an important finding from a bench compatibility test I completed yesterday. Only 600 liters of the stored 900-liter mixture is suitable for this skid. The remaining 300 liters contains a solvent component that the skid's seals are not rated for. The result is still in my lab notebook and hasn't been uploaded to the process file yet, so I'm disclosing it now so we can factor it into the trial planning.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my pre-use inspection findings. During my inspection of the skid, I found that the transfer pump seal must be replaced and pressure-tested before operation. The replacement takes exactly 3 hours, and the seal kit is in the maintenance storeroom. I recorded the finding on a paper inspection sheet that hasn't been entered in the electronic work-order system yet, so I'm disclosing it now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share my permit review findings. This morning I received a clarification from the environmental office regarding the permitting requirements for this solvent recovery trial. My review confirmed that the operation requires ventilation of at least 6 air changes per hour, exactly 2 continuously operating LEL monitors, and a hazardous-waste manifest for the incompatible 300 liters that Jonas just identified. I have not yet filed this clarification with the trial paperwork, so I'm disclosing it now so we can factor these requirements into our planning.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Thank you all for disclosing these findings. Let me summarize where we stand. Jonas, your compatibility test means we can only consider 600 of the 900 liters for this trial — the remaining 300 liters with the incompatible solvent component cannot be run through this skid. Priya, the transfer pump seal needs replacement and pressure-testing before any operation, with a 3-hour downtime using the kit already in the storeroom. Caleb, the environmental requirements are clear: at least 6 air changes per hour ventilation, exactly 2 continuously operating LEL monitors, and a hazardous-waste manifest for the incompatible 300 liters. So here is where we are: the trial is NOT authorized yet. Before I can authorize, the following commitments must be satisfied: (1) Jonas, upload the compatibility test result to the process file. (2) Priya, replace and pressure-test the pump seal — that's 3 hours of maintenance downtime — and enter the inspection finding in the electronic work-order system. (3) Caleb, file the environmental clarification with the trial paperwork and ensure the hazardous-waste manifest for the 300 liters of incompatible solvent is prepared. (4) We need ventilation verification confirming at least 6 air changes per hour. (5) We need confirmation that exactly 2 continuously operating LEL monitors are in place. (6) Closed transfer and documented waste handling must be verified. Once all of these are completed and documented, I will authorize a trial on the 600 compatible liters only. Does anyone have questions or anything else to add before I formalize these commitments?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: No questions from me, Mara. I understand the commitments. I'll upload the compatibility test result to the process file right away so the 600-liter suitability finding is formally documented. One thing to flag for planning purposes: since only 600 of the 900 liters is compatible, the trial scope and any batch documentation should reflect that 600-liter limit clearly, and the 300 liters of incompatible material will need to stay segregated pending the hazardous-waste manifest Caleb is preparing. I'm ready to proceed once all the commitments are satisfied.
